summary: Internal training by Lucia Moretti on individual-animal identifiers, dose-lot traceability and welfare escalation. It defines correction practice, independent QA review and the archive handover required before signed-report release.

properties.title: Animal cards and QA gate training
properties.subject: Animal cards and QA gate training

slides.title: Animal cards: traceability through the QA gate
slides.subtitle:
Osterquill Toxicology Inc | Internal training | 06/14/2022
Lucia Moretti, GLP Quality Assurance and Archive Lead

slides.title: An animal card must identify one animal throughout
bullets: Carry the investigation identifier and individual-animal identifier on every observation sheet.
Link cage or group changes to the same animal; never substitute group identity for individual identity.
Reconcile identifiers at allocation, dosing, sampling and pathology handover.
An unexplained mismatch blocks reconciliation and must be escalated.

slides.title: Minimum contemporaneous entry
bullets: Enter observation date and time, observer identity and the individual-animal identifier.
Describe what was seen before adding interpretation.
Record the action taken and the subsequent condition when welfare intervention occurs.
Use MM/DD/YYYY dates consistently; retain the original entry when correcting an error.

slides.title: Dose-lot traceability
bullets: Link each administration to the prepared dose lot and its preparation observation sheet.
Retain intended dose in mg/kg/day, formulation concentration, administered volume and the body weight used.
Document missed, partial or uncertain administrations individually.
A dose-lot label alone cannot explain which animal received it or when.

slides.title: Welfare escalation must be immediate
bullets: Contact the responsible Study Director and designated welfare personnel when an intervention criterion is met or an unexpected concern arises.
Record the observed signs, notification time, advice received and intervention.
Continue the agreed follow-up observations and link them to the original entry.
Do not postpone welfare action while waiting for an administrative QA gate.
slides.notes: A scheduled review does not replace real-time welfare oversight. Where the responsible person is unavailable, use the approved escalation route.

slides.title: Training exercise: incomplete administration entry

rows: Reconcile the individual identifier against allocation and source observations.
Trace the preparation and administration source; preserve the omission and dated correction.
Establish whether notification or intervention occurred; record the evidence and escalate uncertainty.
Identify the entry as retrospective and state the basis; do not present it as contemporaneous.

slides.notes: Discuss these hypothetical omissions with Rachel Okafor. They are training examples, not findings from an actual investigation.

slides.title: Corrections and study amendments
bullets: Keep the original entry legible; add the correction, date, author and reason.
Do not backdate an observation or replace an uncertain fact with an assumed value.
A planned change to conduct requires a controlled study amendment; an accidental departure requires a documented explanation.
Link the impact assessment to affected animals, dose lots and endpoints.

slides.title: Independent QA gate before signed-report release
bullets: Reconcile animal identifiers and dose-lot links from source observations to report tables.
Check that welfare notifications, departures and corrective actions remain visible.
Confirm control-validity evidence and the stated GLP scope; keep exploratory work separately identified.
The Study Director resolves scientific findings; Lucia Moretti documents independent QA review and outstanding issues.
Unresolved traceability issues must be addressed before release authorization.

slides.title: Archive handover and daily practice
bullets: Transfer signed reports with source indexes, animal cards, observation sheets, study amendments and QA evidence.
Preserve version and approval history so the released report can be reconstructed.
Keep access and retrieval links controlled; do not replace originals with a convenient summary.
Before leaving an entry: can another reader identify the animal, dose lot, observation and action?
Escalate a missing link while the people and source evidence are available.
